items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: So I really got my New York education from Davey. He showed me how to scuffle and he showed me who the interesting people were

ctx.x: Well when I got out of the Army, I was here for like a three day pass in the Army and a quick visit once before out of high school. But I went back to Seattle and re-entered the University of Washington. And this time instead of living at home I moved in to be closer to the campus. A friend had a houseboat on Lake Union that was full of musicians, and I lived there. And I met a drummer there who had been out on the road with bands and came from Olympia, Washington, but he’d been living in New York and he knew the…

ever addressed. So I got to a point with him where I couldn’t stand my day job, and decided that I couldn’t go there anymore. It was just emotionally too shattering to go into that atmosphere every day. So without my day job, then I fell behind on my payments to my therapist, and he suggested that I go out and get another job and live my life and maybe I could afford to talk to a therapist sometime in the future. So I did. I scuffled around New York. And actually I was very lucky to have fallen in with Dave…

Greenwell, wonderful tenor player who had been living in Seattle for a long time; and a trumpet player named Marty Bell, who is still around in Florida someplace; and a piano player named John Vincent Brooks, who had been the arranger for Randy Brooks’ band when Buzzy was on that band. Buzzy Bridgeford was his name. And he couldn’t hire a bass player, the boss wouldn’t go for another rhythm instrument. So he goes back up with this quartet, and he tells me when he leaves, he said “look, we’re going to be up there…
